design_critique:
1) The stated mechanism for the line losses is wrong. The rationale says that with 0.015 m spacing the sensors at +/-0.015 m see no tape when the robot is centred. The tape half-width is 0.0125 m and a 0.008 m footprint centred at 0.015 m spans 0.011 to 0.019 m, so it overlaps the tape by about 0.0015 m, roughly 19 percent reading. It is not zero. The outer sensors at +/-0.03 m do read zero when centred, but that is a different claim.
2) The proposed array (+/-0.016 m, 0.008 m footprints) reduces the lateral range over which any sensor sees tape. The outer edge is at 0.020 m, so the tape is fully out of view once the centre offset exceeds about 0.0325 m. With iteration 4's +/-0.03 m array (outer edge 0.034 m) the threshold was about 0.0465 m. The change therefore makes line loss more likely at moderate offsets, which is the opposite of the stated goal of fewer line-loss events. The robot then recovers through last_direction at throttle 0.35, which is slow, before it reaches the 0.06 m off-track limit. The draft does not acknowledge this trade-off.
3) The change to 0.008 m spacing puts the inner sensors fully on the tape when centred (about +/-0.008 m centres, footprint 0.008 m, edge at 0.0125 m). That is a real improvement in graded signal near centre. However, it is only a gain if the outer sensors still cover the range of offsets the robot actually reaches. The draft does not show that max_error (0.060 to 0.067 across all tracks) falls within the inner-sensor range.
4) The 'one group at a time' framing does not match the design. Spacing and ki change together in one candidate. If the result is worse, the race cannot say which change caused it, which is the same confounding the draft criticised in earlier iterations.
5) ki 0.05 to 0.10 is not a meaningful change. With the integral clamped at +/-2, ki contributes at most 0.2 turn units (about 70 PWM) instead of 0.1. The draft does not estimate the size of the motor-mismatch offset in signal units, so there is no evidence the larger ki removes it. Holding kp at 1.5 means a steady offset still needs a steady signal, which proportional action can only supply at a steady error.
6) base_speed 1.4 is kept, although the progress reached in iterations 3 and 4 was limited by speed on the s-bend and by line loss on the oval. Completion needs about 1.5 m/s average over 4 to 5 m in 3 s. The draft does not estimate the time budget at 1.4 (PWM duty 70 percent), so a finish is unlikely even if the line is held.
7) kd 0.6 is retained with no evidence that more kd helps. Steering oscillation rose when kd went from 0.3 to 0.5 (iteration 1 to 2) and fell when it was reduced (iteration 2 to 3). The draft cites no test that isolates kd.
rationale_critique:
1) The rationale's central claim, that the spread causes the line losses, rests on a miscalculation. The centre sensor reads the tape and the outer sensors at +/-0.015 m still read about 19 percent (see design critique). The argument is therefore not established.
2) 'Iteration 4 showed these gains are workable' overstates the evidence. Iteration 4 finished 1 of 60 trials, and the best score reached was 97. Its gains did not show that they work across tracks.
3) The 'one group at a time' label contradicts the candidate, which changes sensor geometry and ki in the same race.
4) The expected result (fewer line losses, max_error below 0.06, progress above 0.3, oscillation lower) is stated with no model or prior run behind any single value. It does not account for the reduced sensor range, which should make line losses more frequent at moderate offsets.
5) No success thresholds are set that would show whether the sensor change, rather than the ki change, did the work. The next iteration therefore cannot attribute the result.
6) The rationale does not address the time budget. Completion is worth 500 points and needs progress 0.995 within 3.0 s, which requires about 1.5 m/s. Keeping base_speed at 1.4 without an estimate of the finish time leaves that trade-off unexamined.
7) The rationale is internally inconsistent on kd: it treats the sharper signal from the smaller footprint as a reason to raise kd, but it does not show that the smaller footprint produces a sharper signal, and kd has not been shown to reduce oscillation.
